questions.text: A system administrator is investigating a computer that is performing significantly slower than normal. To get a quick overview of what is currently consuming system resources, the administrator issues the ps command. What is the primary type of information that the ps command will display to help the administrator in this situation?
questions.explanation: ps is a process snapshot: PID, terminal, cumulative CPU TIME and command. It doesn't report RAM totals, disk usage or network interface status (that's free, df and ifconfig/ip).

questions.text: A student needs to change the filename myfile.sh to myfile_renamed.sh inside their current working directory. In Linux, the mv command is used both for moving files between directories and for renaming files within a directory.
questions.explanation: Linux has no separate rename command for this; mv myfile.sh myfile_renamed.sh renames in place, and mv myfile.sh ../Desktop/ moves it.

questions.text: An application executes a mathematical operation inside a try block that triggers a ZeroDivisionError, executing the corresponding except block followed by a finally block. The code inside the finally block executes upon completion regardless of whether an exception occurred or was handled.
questions.explanation: finally always runs after the try/except, whether an exception was raised, handled or not. It's typically used for cleanup like closing files.

questions.text: A script receives raw CSV text "apple,banana,cherry". The program needs to split this text into individual list items and then join them into a single string formatted as "apple & banana & cherry". Which method combination correctly accomplishes this transformation?
questions.explanation: .split(",") turns the string into ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'], and " & ".join(fruits) glues the list back together with the separator, giving 'apple & banana & cherry' (verified by running it). The other options reverse the methods or use ones that don't do this (strip trims ends, replace needs two arguments, strings have no append).

questions.text: A cash register software asks the cashier for a product's base price using base_price = float(input("Enter base price: ")). Why is the float() function necessary here?
options: Python variables cannot store numbers unless wrapped in float().
The input() function automatically returns an integer, which cannot be multiplied by decimals.
The input() function returns data as a string literal, which must be converted to a float for tax calculation math.
The float() function formats the text output displayed on the console screen.
questions.explanation: input() always returns a str, so float() converts it to a number before doing math on it. Python variables can hold any numeric type without wrapping, and integers multiply by decimals just fine.

questions.text: A system administrator issues the apt-get upgrade command on a Linux operating system. What is the purpose of this command?
options: Every application installed will update itself to the latest version.
Operating system updates are downloaded and will be installed.
A specific application named upgrade will be installed.
The remote repository of applications and dependencies will be updated to the latest version.
questions.explanation: apt-get upgrade downloads and installs newer versions of the installed packages, including OS packages. Refreshing the repository package lists is apt-get update, apps don't run their own updaters, and "upgrade" is a subcommand, not a package name.
